explanation: Lausanne is the only peace of the First World War settlement negotiated with the defeated side rather than presented to it, and the reason is on the battlefield: the Greek army had been driven out of Anatolia in 1922 and Britain would not fight at Chanak to hold the terms of Sèvres. What the treaty conceded — full sovereignty in Anatolia and eastern Thrace, no Armenian state, no Kurdistan, the capitulations abolished — is the nationalist programme, and the compulsory exchange of populations that came with it was the price the victory was settled at.
